blockers.title: Lockstep pin never reads the production terminal_statuses const — hardcoded test-local copy; the claimed guard cannot bite on const drift
blockers.evidence: const terminal_statuses: List(String) = [ "form_completed", ... ] (private) at application_detail_handler.gleam:1286; test declares its own `let terminal = [...]` at application_detail_handler_test.gleam:596 — the test imports only application_detail_handler/application/sql and never references the const. Arch doc claim: "A lockstep unit test pins the timeline's DB-string terminal_statuses list to the shared fn."
blockers.detail: The PR's own spec and the architecture amendment claim the lockstep pin ties the production DB-string list to the shared fn. The test pins its own hardcoded copy instead — editing terminal_statuses (used at line 1454 for timeline terminal entries) fails nothing. This is the exact mirror-drift pattern AR-RC13 names as the bug class.
blockers.recommended_fix: Export the const (pub) or a pub accessor fn from application_detail_handler, iterate the REAL list in the lockstep test both directions, and make the arch-doc claim match the implementation.

warnings.title: verify_payload_has_no_internal_fields has zero production call sites — item 1 hardening is test-only
warnings.evidence: grep across server/src: callers of verify_payload_has_no_internal_fields exist only in server/test/application/application_detail_handler_test.gleam (407-442) plus the definition. Doc comment claims "a spoofed/malformed payload can't leak internals" — true only if the fn runs.
warnings.detail: Pre-existing wiring gap (RC4.1), but the PR extends this fn and its claim. The §4.2 SQL-boundary strip is the live defense (integration-proven), so no live leak; the belt-and-braces guard never runs in production.
warnings.recommended_fix: Wire the re-verify into the detail serialization path (fail closed), or correct the doc comment to state the guard is test-enforced-only.

warnings.title: trigger.gleam keeps a second unpinned server-side terminality list — the 'terminality has ONE home' claim is false while it exists
warnings.evidence: fn is_terminal(status: String) -> Bool { list.contains( [ "form_completed", "unreachable", "refused", "objected", "manual_recorded", "failed", "completed", "partial" ], status ) } — none of the truth-table, lockstep, or lint layers reads it.
warnings.detail: The AR-RC13 amendment claims terminality has a single shared home. This pre-existing private list drives find_live_row_for_slot; a new terminal status in shared diverges here silently.
warnings.recommended_fix: Rewrite trigger.is_terminal to consume shared status_from_string + is_terminal_status, or add a pin iterating this list against the shared fn.

warnings.title: Hooks lint evadable by list shape — multiline construction and non-final list position both pass CI (sandbox-verified)
warnings.evidence: marker = action + "]"; if marker not in line: continue — sandbox: multiline [RefcheckTakeOver, RefcheckSubstitute,] exits 0; [RefcheckTakeOver, RefcheckSkip] exits 0; the historical single-line shape exits 1 (verified).
warnings.detail: The guard catches the exact RC4.3-r1 shape but is formatting-dependent: a reordered or reformatted re-derivation ships past lint and format-check. The distinguishing panel tests remain as backstop for the historical statuses.
warnings.recommended_fix: Match governed identifiers at word boundaries regardless of line/position (keep the pattern-arm `->` exemption), and consider a CI negative-control fixture feeding historical shapes to the lint.

warnings.title: outcome_from_string is orphaned in production; the optional fn's 15-arm mapping is pinned for only 2 known values — three hand-copied outcome tables with no exhaustive lockstep pin
warnings.evidence: Repo-wide grep: outcome_from_string has zero non-test callers after the encoder switched; its doc claims 'non-wire callers' that do not exist. outcome_from_string_optional duplicates the 15 arms; the new test pins '', one unknown, and two known values only.
warnings.detail: A future outcome enum addition (expand-then-contract is the norm here) updated in encode_outcome/outcome_from_string but missed in the optional fn silently encodes as null on the wire — the same lockstep-drift class AR-RC13 names, in the codec that pins the unknown-outcome contract.
warnings.recommended_fix: Derive outcome_from_string from the optional fn (Some -> o; None -> OutcomeUnreachable) so one mapping exists, and add an exhaustive pin: every all_outcomes() entry through encode_outcome |> outcome_from_string_optional == Some(outcome).

notes.title: lint_refcheck_hooks false-positives on a legit non-hook case nested inside a hooks gate
notes.evidence: Sandbox-verified: case call.hooks.can_take_over { True -> case call.status { unreachable -> [RefcheckTakeOver] } } exits 1 — the shallower non-hook `case` disconnects the scan despite the outer hook gate holding.
notes.detail: A legitimate future refactor (status sub-menu inside a hooks gate — legal under AR-RC13: statuses pick menus, hooks gate content) fails CI and forces restructuring.
notes.recommended_fix: Track hook-case open/close depth explicitly instead of bailing on the first shallower non-hook case; document the nesting constraint.

notes.title: written_response_disclaimer em-dash sits outside the lint scope with an undocumented exemption
notes.evidence: const written_response_disclaimer = "Written response, provenance-checked — not verbally confirmed..." renders to landlords via display_disclaimer (client reference_panel.gleam:1770). The string is spec-verbatim (architecture-reference-checking-v1:1037 defines it), so exempt-by-construction — but the module is not in the lint's SERVER_INCLUDE and no copy test scans it.
notes.detail: Exemption is legitimate (spec-verbatim) but undocumented; future implementer-authored em-dashes in this module ship unscanned.
notes.recommended_fix: Document the verbatim exemption in the lint's docstring, or add the handler consts to a pinned scan list that whitelists this string.

notes.title: lint_em_dash scanner has two false-negative paths: escaped-quote state toggle and whole-line log-call exemption
notes.evidence: string_literal_em_dashes toggles in_str on every `"` without backslash-escape awareness (unlike strip_comments); LOG_CALL_RE exempts the entire line. Verified: no current line mixes a user-facing em-dash with a log call, so live impact is zero today.
notes.detail: An odd number of escaped quotes in a string flips the scan state and hides a later em-dash; any log call sharing a line exempts the whole line. The console.* alternative is dead (only .gleam scanned).
notes.recommended_fix: Skip backslash-escaped chars in the in_str toggle (mirror strip_comments); scope the log exemption to the call argument; drop console.*.

notes.title: Same-instant mixed-format attempts group into two cadence batches — the new pin covers ordering, not grouping
notes.evidence: group_attempts_by_at groups on the RAW entry.at (no normalize_at): [#(at, entries), ..rest] if at == entry.at. A space-form and T-form attempt at the same instant become two groups → two send entries → mislabeled batches for one send.
notes.detail: Legacy/corrupt rows with mixed formats at the same instant render 'Invitation sent' plus 'co-nudge' for a single send. The new fixture mixes formats at different instants only, so it cannot catch this.
notes.recommended_fix: Group on the normalized key (normalize_at inside group_attempts_by_at) or add a same-instant mixed-format fixture asserting one shared batch label.

notes.title: copy.gleam em-dash enforcement rests on hand-maintained test lists; the lint exempts the module wholesale
notes.evidence: CLIENT_EXCLUDE = {"client/src/copy.gleam"}; inside copy.gleam only refcheck_action_strings() and refcheck_fn_built_labels() (hand-maintained lists) are scanned. The PR correctly added its new fns to the scanned list.
notes.detail: A new implementer-authored const with an em-dash ships unless its author remembers to add it to a scan list — the W5 gap pattern, mitigated here but not closed structurally.
notes.recommended_fix: Narrow the exemption (scan copy.gleam, whitelist the spec-verbatim strings) or generate the scan lists from the module so new strings are covered by default.

notes.title: Amendment register claims §8.2 was amended in place with the unknown-outcome rule, but §8.2 contains no such content
notes.evidence: Register: "Amended in place: ... §8.2 (hooks contract doc: unknown-outcome rule, #607 item 2)." §8.2 as it reads describes only the three hook booleans — no unknown-outcome rule. The named rule exists solely in the shared module doc (ReferenceCallHooks).
notes.detail: The canon's claimed in-place amendment was never written; future readers following the register will not find the rule where it points.
notes.recommended_fix: Add the unknown-outcome rule to §8.2 (hooks from status only; unrecognised outcome encodes absent, never the fallback), or fix the register entry to point at the shared module doc.

notes.title: Substitute message-payload construction is shape-exempt from the hooks lint — its gate is code-review-only
notes.evidence: UserChoseRefcheckAction(call.reference_call_id, RefcheckSubstitute) inside view_substitute_surface_open, which is only reachable through case call.hooks.can_substitute_referee (line 1029). The lint's RefcheckSubstitute] marker never matches this shape (documented exemption).
notes.detail: A future body-surface re-derivation via message payload escapes the CI lint; the panel distinguishing tests remain as backstop.
notes.recommended_fix: Extend the lint to require UserChoseRefcheckAction take-over/substitute constructions to sit inside the hook-gated render path, or move construction below the gate.
